# 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Jehoshaphat his son succeeded him as king and strengthened his position against Israel.

**2** He stationed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and placed garrisons throughout Judah and in the towns of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.

**3** The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he followed the earlier ways of his father David. He did not consult the Baals

**4** but sought the God of his father and followed His commands rather than the practices of Israel.

**5** The LORD established the kingdom firmly in his hands. All Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had great wealth and honor.

**6** His heart was devoted to the ways of the LORD; furthermore, he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.

**7** In the third year of his reign he sent his officials — Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah — to teach in the towns of Judah.

**8** With them were the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah — and the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

**9** They taught throughout Judah, taking the Book of the Law of the LORD with them. They went to all the towns of Judah and taught the people.

**10** The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, so that none of them went to war against Jehoshaphat.

**11** Some Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabs brought him flocks: 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats.

**12** Jehoshaphat grew more and more powerful. He built forts and supply cities in Judah.

**13** He had large forces in Judah's cities. In Jerusalem were his elite warriors, mighty men of valor.

**14** Their enrollment by families was as follows: From Judah, commanders of thousands — Adnah the chief, with 300,000 fighting men;

**15** next, Jehohanan the commander, with 280,000;

**16** next, Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered himself for the LORD's service, with 200,000 fighting men.

**17** From Benjamin — Eliada, a mighty warrior, with 200,000 men armed with bows and shields;

**18** next, Jehozabad, with 180,000 men equipped for battle.

**19** These served the king directly, in addition to those he had stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **17:6**: "His heart was devoted to the ways of the LORD" — the Hebrew word here usually means "proud" (gavah), but the Chronicler uses it positively. Jehoshaphat was proudly righteous. His ambition ran in God's direction.

- **17:7-9**: This is one of the most innovative moves by any king in Chronicles: a traveling teaching commission carrying the Torah to every city. Jehoshaphat understood that national faith requires national education.

- **17:10**: "The fear of the LORD fell on all the surrounding kingdoms" — not fear of Jehoshaphat's army, but fear of Jehoshaphat's God. When you get the internal right, the external takes care of itself.


— PNEUMA
